strategies.title: Revise within the supplied record
strategies.input_summary: All entities, local rules, page references and proceedings are fictional. Ridge Nursery sought a county conditional-use permit for a plant greenhouse. The assumed applicable ordinance requires findings on traffic safety and compatibility; no fundamental vested right is asserted. At the administrative hearing, Ridge submitted a traffic memorandum at administrative record(AR)40–46 proposing timed delivery windows. A neighbor described a blind driveway curve at AR 70–72. The county’s resolution at AR 100–101 denied the permit using only the ordinance’s conclusions, with no explanation of which traffic or compatibility facts it found or why delivery conditions were inadequate. Ridge objected to missing findings at AR 95 and renewed that issue in its superior-court writ petition at clerk’s transcript(CT)20–24. The superior court denied relief, stating at CT 80 that the neighbor evidence could support denial without identifying findings in the resolution. A timely appeal from that final judgment is assumed for this exercise. Ridge now has a new traffic survey, prepared after judgment, that was not in the administrative record.
assumptions: All parties, facts and record locators are fictional.

## Preservation

## Standard Of Review

## Argument

## Relief
Order immediate issuance of the permit.

revised.response_text:
## Issues
Whether the writ judgment should be reversed because the county’s resolution failed to disclose findings that connect the admitted traffic and compatibility evidence to denial, preventing meaningful review. Ridge seeks reconsideration on a lawful explanation, not an appellate selection of its preferred traffic expert.

## Preservation
Ridge raised the missing-findings objection at AR 95 and in the writ petition at CT 20–24. The resolution appears at AR 100–101 and the trial court’s reasoning at CT 80. Those are supplied fictional record anchors. The postjudgment survey is excluded from this argument; no exception permitting its use or preserved request for additional evidence is assumed. Timeliness and the final-judgment posture are stipulated solely for this exercise and require verification in any actual matter.

## Standard Of Review
CCP 1094.5 distinguishes review of findings, evidentiary support and agency discretion. With no fundamental vested right asserted here, Ridge frames the evidentiary issue under substantial-evidence review, not free reweighing. The primary challenge is instead the legal adequacy of the explanation necessary for that review. Topanga requires a discernible connection between evidence, findings and decision, while recognizing deference to supported administrative findings.

## Argument
The traffic memorandum proposed timed deliveries; the neighbor described a blind curve. Either account may matter, and Ridge does not claim that its memorandum automatically prevails. The defect is that the resolution merely repeats traffic-safety and compatibility conclusions without saying what facts were found, how the delivery proposal was evaluated, or which reason supports denial. On this assumed record the reviewing court must supply its own route from competing evidence to outcome.
The county’s strongest response is that the resolution and record, read together and with appropriate deference, sufficiently reveal the basis for its action. Ridge must meet that response by pointing to the actual absence of explanatory findings, not a demand for ideal drafting or a finding on every evidentiary detail. If the full resolution incorporates a reasoned staff report omitted from this packet, Ridge’s premise may fail. The supplied resolution contains no such incorporation.
The superior court’s statement that neighbor evidence could support denial does not itself establish the findings the agency made. Remand would let the county articulate and reconsider its own reasoning within its lawful discretion. It would not resolve whether the greenhouse should ultimately receive a permit.

## Relief
Reverse the writ judgment and direct appropriate relief setting aside the inadequately explained decision and returning the matter for lawful agency reconsideration under CCP 1094.5. Do not direct permit issuance on this packet. The county could again deny the permit with adequate findings and support. Counsel must confirm the complete record, precise standard, preservation and remedy before filing.

claims.claim: CCP 1094.5 addresses evidentiary/findings review and remand, preserving legally vested agency discretion; the applicable evidentiary standard depends on the right and proceeding.

Topanga requires reviewable agency findings connecting evidence to decision, with reasonable doubts resolved in favor of agency findings; it does not require courts to speculate about an unstated path.
